audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer carried a blanket 'Skill' on all seven rows while content win[N] read Xerath on all seven and the packet levelChart agrees with content. The page answered 'who wins Level 1' two different ways.
audit.why: Xerath Q reaches 750 and E 1050 against Winds of War at 825 with no repeatable way to close: Justice Punch is 650 and 11s at rank 1, Shield of Durand needs 275. At 52.63% the data agrees the lane is Xerath's.
audit.corrected: All seven phases[N].side set to Xerath, matching win[N] (already Xerath) and the existing whys, which already describe Xerath winning each stage.
sources: kits: Xerath Q 750 / E 1050, Galio Q 825 / E 650

audit.whatIsWrong: The spike write-ups never carried Hero's Entrance's cooldown, which is the number that decides how often he can leave the lane.
audit.why: Hero's Entrance is 180/160/140s and reaches 4000/4750/5500 units — one roam every three minutes early, not an on-demand threat.
audit.corrected: Stated the 180/160/140s cooldown in breakdown.cooldowns so the 'match his push' advice has a timer on it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was never stated: Shield of Durand is a charged taunt and Justice Punch a knockup, so either one ends Rite of the Arcane mid-channel; and his Colossal Smash passive is an auto reset, so the wind-up is the tell.
audit.why: The owner kit flags R channel/interruptible; Galio's W is flagged hardCC and E knockup. brief.missingInteractions flags autoreset-burst-tell.
audit.corrected: cooldowns now names the taunt at 18s rank 1, the knockup at 11s rank 1, and the fact that either cancels your R.
sources: brief.enemyKit W flags.hardCC cd 18/17/16/15/14, E flags.knockup cd 11/10/9/8/7

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns held no digit (lintFindings COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT); dontsFull[1].d called Shocking Orb a fourteen-second spell when it is 13s at rank 1 down to 11s.
audit.why: Justice Punch at 11s rank 1 against Shocking Orb at 13s means his engage comes back first — that gap is the whole step-up decision.
audit.corrected: Both fields rewritten with sourced numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim, dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim, and dontsFull[0].d was a name-swappable line that said nothing about Galio (lintFindings COPY_PASTE_BLEED).
audit.why: Each body answered a different question from its title.
audit.corrected: All three rewritten from Galio's ranges and cooldowns.

edits.before: - Galio Justice Punch: matchup-defining — His dash knockup — he has no engage while it is down. Check it before every step-up. - E Shocking Orb is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Justice Punch: 11s at rank 1, 650 units — down, he cannot reach you at all. - Shield of Durand is 18s at rank 1; taunt or knockup ends your R channel. - Hero's Entrance is 180/160/140s: once he leaves, mid is yours for minutes.

edits.before: Galio wins by landing Justice Punch, denying your pattern, and cashing the all-in before your pattern matures.
edits.after: Galio wins by knocking you up with Justice Punch into a Shield of Durand taunt, holding you still for his team.

edits.before: His dash knockup — he has no engage while it is down. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Q reaches 750, Winds of War 825, Justice Punch 650 — poke from the outer band and he answers with nothing.

edits.before: Q the last-hit from beyond his answer range, W the lateral dodge, and walk — a one-way trade he can only end by leaving the lane.
edits.after: Justice Punch knocks up the first champion it meets, so stun him in the wind-up — landing short, his 275-unit taunt never reaches.

edits.before: That’s Galio’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Inside 650 units his dash simply collects you — Q from the far band or not at all.

edits.before: Your E is a single 'no' per fourteen seconds — spent on poke, every assassin and fighter in the lobby hears the silence.
edits.after: Shocking Orb is 13s at rank 1 against an 11s Justice Punch — spend it on poke and his engage is back before your answer is.

edits.before: Spending E on chip and then watching the dash you bought it for arrive on schedule — the stun is your only 'no' and everyone knows it.
edits.after: Standing on the wave puts you inside 650 units of a loaded Justice Punch, and the taunt that follows holds you for his whole rotation.

edits.before: If Galio opens the score, reset expectations and respect Justice Punch doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with max-range Qs and stay relevant through R snipes.
edits.after: A fed Galio survives your rotation and still taunts, so stop contesting the wave and farm the back of it at 750 range. Track Hero's Entrance at 140s and stay relevant through R snipes.

notes: Full layer had the blanket 'Skill 5/10' on all seven rows while content win[N] and the packet both read Xerath — side edits only, since win[N] is already the value I am moving side to. Ratings left untouched (5/10 and 6/10): the kit does not tell me whether the number describes the owner's strength or the stage margin, and the chart rule says leave rather than guess — flagged here rather than fixed. Kit flag contradiction: Galio's E carries a 'terrain' flag, but Riot's own text for Justice Punch says only that he steps back, charges and knocks up the first champion he encounters — no terrain is created. I did not write the missingInteractions 'terrain-cuts-retreat' line for that reason; the flag looks like a tooltip-parsing misfire.
